Which regime governs the lease: a lease concluded before the 2005 reform of the Commercial Code (renewal right, notice to vacate, eviction indemnity) or one concluded after it (term-limited lease, departure at term without indemnity unless agreed): the date of the contract decides.

Basis of the renewal right under the old regime: the premises must house a business (fonds de commerce) exploited by the tenant, with the required minimum period of continuous exploitation (shorter for a written lease, longer for an oral one).
Form of the lease after 2005: must the commercial lease be in an official (notarial) deed, and what follows if it is not (nullity or loss of the commercial regime)?

Notice to vacate (congé): must be served by an extrajudicial act (bailiff), a set time ahead (six months in my memory), state the grounds for refusing renewal, and reproduce the text that tells the tenant to sue within a set time; what sanction attaches to a notice lacking these (nullity).

Time limit for the tenant to contest the notice or claim the eviction indemnity: from the date of the notice, a short forfeiture period (three months in my memory) after which the tenant loses the right to renewal and indemnity; check the exact article and its counting.

Refusal of renewal: the lessor may refuse, but must pay the eviction indemnity equal to the harm caused by non-renewal (market value of the business, moving costs, reinstallation), unless an exception applies.

Exceptions to the indemnity: a serious and legitimate ground against the tenant (non-payment of rent, breach of the lease) only if the breach continued or was renewed more than a month after a formal notice to stop it; demolition of an insalubrious or dangerous building; reconstruction or personal occupation with priority rights.
Right of the tenant to stay in the premises until the indemnity is paid, and the lessor's right to withdraw the refusal (droit de repentir) within a set period.

Elements to prove for an eviction claim by the lessor: the lease and its date and rent; the lessor's title or standing; the notice to vacate and its date and service; the expiry of the notice period; the ground relied on (unpaid rent, end of term for a post-2005 lease).

Elements to prove for an indemnity claim by the tenant: the lease, its date, the exploitation of the business for the required period, the registration in the commercial register, the notice/refusal of renewal, the amount of harm.
Unpaid rent as a ground: formal notice to pay (by bailiff) and the one-month period before the lessor may rely on it; any rescission clause in the lease.

Who bears the proof: the lessor proves the lease and the notice; the tenant proves the exploitation period and the harm; the lessor proves the serious and legitimate ground that removes the indemnity.
Proof of the lease: written official deed for post-2005 leases; commercial freedom of proof for the business elements.
Court and section: the ordinary court (tribunal), commercial section; check whether commercial leases fall within the specialised commercial courts (law of 2022) - in my memory they do not.
Territorial jurisdiction: the court of the place where the leased property lies (lease of real property, commercial leases included) under the Code of Civil and Administrative Procedure.

Exits from the ordinary courts: a public body as lessor (State, wilaya, commune, public administrative body) may move the case to the administrative court; urgent eviction of an occupant without title belongs to the summary judge.

Limitation of the claim for rent arrears: periodic renewable rights (five years in my memory, Civil Code); and a general limitation for actions under the commercial-lease chapter (two years in my memory) - check.
Counting of periods: by days, months or years under the CCAP rules; the starting day not counted; the last day extended if a holiday.
Does the court raise forfeiture of the tenant's right of its own motion, or only on a plea?

Prior steps before filing: the notice to vacate (lessor) or the request for renewal (tenant); a formal notice for unpaid rent; no compulsory conciliation before the ordinary court in a commercial-lease case (check).
Is publication of the petition at the land registry required? Probably not for an eviction claim, which does not seek to annul or rescind a published right - check the module.
Required documents: the lease (official deed if post-2005), the bailiff's record of the notice to vacate, extract of the commercial register, proof of title of the lessor, proof of unpaid rent.
Petition formal elements: the general CCAP requirements (court, parties, facts, requests, documents, Arabic, fees).

Boundaries: residential or professional leases under the Civil Code (not commercial); management contracts (location-gérance) of a business; occupation without title; lease of land without a business; leases of public domain; leases of premises for craft activities (also covered?).
Accessory requests: rent arrears, occupation indemnity after the term, damages for delay, provisional execution, costs, appointment of an expert to assess the indemnity.

Amendments in memory: law 05-02 of 6 February 2005 (article 187 bis and following); law 22-13 of 2022 on specialised commercial courts; Civil Code amendments of 2007 on leases (article 467 bis and the written form).
Request kind eviction: the lessor's claim; request kind damages: the tenant's eviction indemnity; request kind payment: the lessor's claim for unpaid rent.
